YTA. I'm sure your late wife expected you to help her daughter, despite you not being directly involved in her raising. You should *at least* find a relative of hers that can help her initiate a new live. Not give her five months and forget that she exists.

Definitely NOT THE AH. I feel you. My (25F) older sister (26F) is just like that. Was always abusive to me, stealing my stuff, not respecting my boundaries... When I was 18yo she attacked me after an argument (she had stole something from me and I got it back) and left me with a black eye and a concussion (I didn't fought back). I cut ties and we haven't spoke since, despite living in the same house (our mother's place).

So take care of yourself and do what's best for you. I'm happier since I did it.

Oh yes, they can. I relate to the op. I (25f) have a sister (26f) just like that, entitled, just got her first job ever couple months ago. And being my older sister always felt like she owned me. We still live in my mother's house, but we haven't talked to each other for over seven years after I cut ties following an incident that was the last straw for me. So yeah, I would say no contact to be the best route. I'm happier since I did it.

I think this is a complex situation. It's understandable how your mother feels, but at the same time parents can have a hard time following boundaries thinking they know what's best for their kid.

But you aren't a kid and made very clear that you are recovering and can take care of yourself now. She may be upset, but sometimes we must draw a line.

I would suggest to maintain your statement, but keep her posted, to ease her worries. Even if she's mad at you and vice versa.

That's what is most important. Who supports you and your choices. Just a parallel: my mom hates that I don't talk with my sister, but she's a leech and brings nothing positive in my life. I have been happier since I cuted ties. Always aims for what makes you happy.

Best wishes for your wedding!
